title: Erdős #131: Non-Dividing Sets Growth Rate
description: Formalizes Erdős Problem #131: estimate F(N) = max size of A ⊆ {1,...,N} where no element divides the sum of other distinct elements. Defines IsNonDividing predicate, proves the two formulations are not equivalent (counterexample {2,4}), monotonicity of F, and derives the negative resolution: Pham-Zakharov (2024) shows F(N) ≤ N^{1/4+o(1)}, answering Erdős's question negatively. 20 theorems, 6 definitions, 2 axioms.

meta.author: Lean Genius
meta.assumptions: 2 axioms: pham_zakharov_upper_bound (Pham-Zakharov 2024: F(N) ≤ N^{1/4+o(1)}), csaba_lower_bound (Csaba: F(N) >> N^{1/5}).
originalContributions: IsNonDividing: no a ∈ A divides sum of ≥2 distinct elements from A\{a}
IsNonDividingAlt: no a ∈ A divides sum of ANY nonempty subset
nondividingAlt_implies_nondividing: Alt is strictly stronger (proved with counterexample)
nondividing_not_iff_alt: explicit counterexample {2,4} distinguishing the two definitions
F: the maximum non-dividing set size function
original_question_answered_no: Erdős's question is answered negatively (proved from Pham-Zakharov axiom)

overview.historicalContext:
Erdős posed Problem #131 in 1975, asking for an estimate of F(N) — the maximum size of a subset A ⊆ {1,...,N} where no element divides the sum of other distinct elements. Erdős originally believed F(N) might be as small as (log N)^O(1), but Ernst Straus showed this is wrong by constructing sets of size exp((√(2/log 2)+o(1))·√(log N)).

The question 'Is F(N) > N^{1/2-o(1)}?' appeared plausible in light of the ELRSS bound (Erdős, Lev, Rauzy, Sándor, Sárközy, 1999): F(N) < 3√N+1. The ELRSS argument used a connection between non-dividing sets and sequences with no element dividing the sum of any other: if a|Σbᵢ and Σbᵢ/|S| = a, then non-dividing implies non-averaging, giving a foothold for Fourier-analytic bounds.

Pham and Zakharov (2024) dramatically improved this: F(N) ≤ N^{1/4+o(1)}, exploiting the cap set connection more carefully. Cap sets in 𝔽₃ⁿ relate to 3-term arithmetic progressions via Fourier analysis (Gowers, Bourgain); the non-averaging condition translates to cap set bounds, which in turn give polynomial improvements over √N. This answered Erdős's question definitively in the negative.

The problem connects to Erdős's broader program on additive structure of integer sets, including Problems #28 (additive bases), #186 (non-averaging sets), and the theory of Sidon sets.
overview.problemStatement: Estimate F(N) = max{|A| : A ⊆ {1,...,N}, A is non-dividing}. Is F(N) > N^{1/2-o(1)}?
overview.text: A set A is non-dividing if no element a ∈ A divides the sum of any ≥2 other distinct elements from A. This property implies non-averaging: no element is the arithmetic mean of others. F(N) counts the maximum such set. ELRSS (1999) gave F(N) < 3√N+1. Pham-Zakharov (2024) sharpened this dramatically to F(N) ≤ N^{1/4+o(1)}, using the connection to non-averaging sets and cap sets.
overview.proofStrategy: The formalization proceeds in 15 sections. (1) Define IsNonDividing and IsNonDividingAlt, prove the implication (Alt → Standard) and exhibit the counterexample {2,4} showing non-equivalence. (2) Define IsNonAveraging and prove non-dividing implies non-averaging (the key bridge). (3) Define F(N) via a powerset supremum (noncomputable) and prove monotonicity. (4) Axiomatize the Pham-Zakharov 2024 bound F(N) ≤ N^{1/4+o(1)}, then formally derive the negative answer to Erdős's question via rpow monotonicity. (5) Axiomatize Csaba's lower bound; prove the Straus constant √(2/log 2) ∈ (1.6,1.8) from scratch using Taylor approximations for exp. (6) Prove Erdős's original logarithmic conjecture is false using log ≤ x^δ/δ and the Csaba bound. (7-8) Verify concrete non-dividing sets ({2,3}, {2,4,5}, {3,5,11,18}) and counterexamples ({2,3,5}, {3,5,7}). (9) Prove structural constraints: 1 ∉ large non-dividing sets; if 2 ∈ A then |A| ≤ 3. (10) Formally connect F ≤ g and derive the Pham-Zakharov bound for F from the bound for g.
keyInsights: The bridge to non-averaging: if $a = \frac{\Sigma b_i}{k}$, then $a \mid \Sigma b_i$. This converts an averaging violation into a divisibility violation, allowing Fourier-analytic bounds on non-averaging sets to transfer to non-dividing sets.

The two formulations differ: the standard definition requires the subset to have ≥ 2 elements, making {2,4} vacuously non-dividing. The alternative (all nonempty subsets) is strictly stronger — a meaningful distinction for small sets near the extremal construction.

Erdős's original conjecture F(N) < (log N)^O(1) was already disproved by Straus, who found sets of superpolylogarithmic size. The ELRSS 1999 bound F(N) < 3√N was a major improvement; Pham-Zakharov 2024's N^{1/4+o(1)} is a further 50% reduction in the exponent.

The parity constraint: if 2 ∈ A, then |A| ≤ 3. Among any 4 elements with 2 present, three non-2 elements must include two of the same parity; their sum is even. This illustrates why constructing large non-dividing sets avoids even elements.
Element 1 is always excluded from non-dividing sets of size ≥ 3: since 1 | (any sum), the condition fails immediately. So large non-dividing sets live in {2,...,N}, not {1,...,N}.

The gap 1/4 - 1/5 = 1/20 between polynomial bound exponents (Pham-Zakharov vs Csaba) leaves open whether F(N) is closer to N^{1/4} or to the subpolynomial Straus bound exp(c√(log N)). The correct growth rate is unknown.
prerequisites: Cap sets and non-averaging sets: connections to combinatorics

conclusion.summary: Erdős #131 formalized: IsNonDividing defined, counterexample distinguishing two formulations, F(N) function, original question answered NO via Pham-Zakharov 2024. 20 theorems, 556 lines, 2 axioms.
conclusion.implications: The Pham-Zakharov result (2024) is very recent and represents a major advance. The connection to non-averaging sets and cap sets is the new technique. The exact growth rate of F(N) between N^{1/5} and N^{1/4} remains open.
openQuestions: Determine the exact growth rate of F(N): is it N^{1/5+o(1)} or some other power?
Prove the Pham-Zakharov bound without axioms using cap set techniques
Formalize the ELRSS bound F(N) < 3√N+1 (simpler than Pham-Zakharov)

crossReferences.description: Both are Erdős problems on additive structure of integer sets

sections.title: Problem Statement and References
sections.summary: Module header with the full problem statement, known results (ELRSS 1999, Pham-Zakharov 2024, Csaba, Straus), and references to [Er75b], [ELRSS99], [PhZa24], [Gu04].

sections.title: Basic Definitions
sections.summary: Defines IsNonDividing and IsNonDividingAlt, proves the implication Alt → Standard (nondividingAlt_implies_nondividing), with docstring explaining the counterexample {2,4}.

sections.title: Counterexample: Separation of Definitions
sections.summary: nondividing_not_iff_alt exhibits {2,4} as a non-dividing set that is NOT non-dividing-alt, proving the two definitions are inequivalent.

sections.title: Non-Dividing Implies Non-Averaging
sections.summary: Defines IsNonAveraging and proves nondividing_implies_nonaveraging: if a = (Σbᵢ)/k then a|Σbᵢ, so non-dividing is strictly stronger than non-averaging.

sections.title: The Extremal Function F(N)
sections.summary: Defines F(N) as the supremum of cardinalities over non-dividing subsets of {1,...,N} (noncomputable). Proves F_monotonic: N ≤ M implies F(N) ≤ F(M).

sections.title: Upper Bound: Pham-Zakharov 2024
sections.summary: Axiomatizes pham_zakharov_upper_bound (F(N) ≤ N^{1/4+o(1)}). Proves original_question_answered_no: Erdős's question 'Is F(N) > N^{1/2-o(1)}?' is answered NO via a real-analysis contradiction.

sections.title: Lower Bounds: Csaba and Straus
sections.summary: Axiomatizes csaba_lower_bound (F(N) ≫ N^{1/5}). Proves bounds on log 2 via Taylor approximations to exp, establishing the Straus constant √(2/log 2) ∈ (1.6, 1.8).

sections.title: The Open Question and Erdős's Original Conjecture
sections.summary: States erdos_131_open_question. Proves erdos_original_conjecture_false: Erdős's original belief F(N) < (log N)^O(1) is refuted by Csaba's polynomial lower bound via log ≤ x^δ/δ.

sections.title: Small Examples
sections.summary: singleton_nondividing, two_three_nondividing (vacuous), primes_not_nondividing ({2,3,5} fails since 2|8), two_four_five_nondividing ({2,4,5} works, giving F(5) ≥ 3).

sections.title: Structural Results
sections.summary: one_not_in_large_nondividing: 1 cannot appear in a non-dividing set of size ≥ 3. two_in_nondividing_bound: if 2 ∈ A, then |A| ≤ 3 (parity constraint via pigeonhole).

sections.title: Connection to Non-Averaging Sets
sections.summary: Defines g(N) (max non-averaging subset size). Proves F_le_g (F(N) ≤ g(N)) and pham_zakharov_chain: bounds on g transfer to F via the implication non-dividing → non-averaging.

sections.title: Constructive Difficulty
sections.summary: nondividing_hard_to_find: {3,5,7} fails (3|12) and {3,7,11} fails (3|18), illustrating why constructing large non-dividing sets is non-trivial.

sections.title: Parity Constraint for Sets Containing 2
sections.summary: two_in_nondividing_bound (repeated for context): if 2 ∈ A and A is non-dividing, then |A| ≤ 3, proved via parity pigeonhole on A \ {2}.

sections.title: Four-Element Example and Helper Lemma
sections.summary: Helper lemma nondividing_three_subset reduces checking to full+pair sums. three_five_eleven_eighteen_nondividing verifies {3,5,11,18} is non-dividing (F(18) ≥ 4).

sections.title: Exponent Comparisons
sections.summary: quarter_lt_half (1/4 < 1/2), fifth_lt_quarter (1/5 < 1/4), polynomial_exponent_gap (1/4 - 1/5 = 1/20): formalizing the numeric relationships between known bound exponents.
